open_points.subject: Model M12 — StoreHistory
open_points.text: It has no identifier: it is identified by the store that holds it, exactly one per store, and nothing names it — no answer, no record, no audit entry. Registry makes it, with no closure and number 0, in the transaction that makes a new, empty store (State 2 A17 rule 5); it never makes a second one.
open_points.question: When a backup replaces a lost store, is its StoreHistory the same entity continued from the lost store, or a new StoreHistory for the restored store's new history; if it is new, who creates it and from what, given that Registry neither detects the restore nor makes a second one?
options: The backup preserves the same StoreHistory entity, despite loss of later facts and a lower restored sequence number.
The restored store has a new StoreHistory entity initialized from the backup's facts by the owner or restore boundary.
The restored store has a new StoreHistory entity that Registry is deemed to mint when it starts on the backup.
open_points.default_guess: Treat restoration as creating a new StoreHistory entity outside Registry, initialized from the backup's facts, because R0-89 says the restored store begins its own history and scopes the numbering guarantee to each history.

witness.initial: A store's StoreHistory has reached audit sequence 10; the latest available backup contains the same record at sequence 7.
events: The store is lost after sequence 10 was committed.
The owner puts the sequence-7 backup in its place outside Registry.
Registry starts on the restored store without knowing that restoration occurred.
outcomes: The restored record is the same StoreHistory entity, so its last sequence number has moved from 10 down to 7 despite the statement that it is never lowered.
The restored record is a new StoreHistory entity for the new store history, but it was not made with a new empty store by Registry and the text does not identify who minted it.
witness.observer: The owner inspecting audit numbering after recovery, and any later audit append that uses the restored sequence.

open_points.subject: Model M12 — StoreHistory
open_points.text:
The two facts change for different reasons — every audit append, and the
one import — but they are kept in one record because they share one scope
and one life, the store's history (R0-89), and no caller reads either apart
from the store it is in. Each is changed only by its own transaction, and
neither changes the other.
open_points.rule: Не смешивай таблицы только потому, что у них похожая форма. Решение о merge/split принимается по change-axis: что меняется вместе и по одной причине.
open_points.question: The passage must split facts with independent change axes into separate models, or state a change-axis under which they change together and for one reason.
